summary.title: How I Read
summary.one_liner: Rob Henderson's personal reading habits: slow, note-taking reading of many books at once, a daily morning reading routine, and why he prefers reading over audiobooks and podcasts.
takeaways: Reading slowly with notes, underlining and pauses, and reading several books concurrently, is his approach; he is not a speed reader and says there is no secret.
Reading is preferred over audiobooks and podcasts for deep engagement and retention; podcasts are best used to supplement a book being read.
Build the habit first: start with a small daily reading target (one page, then five, then ten) rather than focusing on volume.
Reduce phone distractions: remove games and social apps, keep a 'kale phone' for useful tools, and charge the phone away from the bed.
Don't finish every book; skim, shelve and return to books later, and expect most reading to be low yield before finding valuable material.
summary.summary: This personal essay by Rob Henderson describes how he reads a large number of books: slowly, with annotations, several books at a time, and with a daily routine of reading with morning coffee and before bed. He argues that reading beats audiobooks, TV and podcasts for serious engagement, quoting Naval Ravikant, Byrne Hobart, Tyler Cowen, Janan Ganesh and James Clear. The piece also covers phone habits, buying and trading books, and abandoning books that do not hold attention. It is opinion and anecdote rather than a formal tutorial.
